sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 19.09.2022 at about 7.15 a.m, the petitioner who was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EQ-2880 on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 road,
dashed against a Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 that was negligently parked in the middle of the said road without putting any indicators or signal opposite to La-Classic Hotel,
Yadavanahalli village, Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 road, Bengaluru and thereby sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was rushed to Best Hospital, Bengoauru, where he has taken treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgery.
The accidental injuries have resulted in permanent disablement to him.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident as the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in the alleged accident in order to wangle an award.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured lorry is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road and he was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
In fact the petitioner was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.

Without prejudice to the above contention it is averred that the insured Eicher vehicle did not have permit & fitness certificate to ply in a public place and the driver thereof did not possess valid & effective driving licence.
In fact the owner of the insured vehicle had knowingly entrusted his vehicle to a person who had no valid and effective DL.
On account of willful breach of the terms and conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of Sec's 134(c), 158(6), 150, 159 of the MV Act, 1988 is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred due to the negligent parking of the driver of the Eicher canter.
The respondent No.2 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 and was duly insured with the 1st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is stated that the driver of the canter vehicle possessing valid and effective DL on the date of accident.
It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the 2nd Respondent - insurance company.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :

sentences.text: 2 ISSUES 1

Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a road traffic accident on 19.09.2022 at about 7.15 a.m., Opposite to LA Classic Hotel situated on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 road, Yadavanahalli village, Bengaluru District and sustained grievous injuries due to actionable negligence of the driver of Eicher canter lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 ?
2 Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3 What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as P.W1.
Ex's.P1 to 9 were marked.

The Assistant Legal Manager of respondent No.1 company examined as RW.1.
7.
Heard arguments of both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record and arguments.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.27,00,000/- together.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, on 19.09.2022 at about 7.15 a.m, the petitioner who was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EQ-2880 on Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 road, dashed against a Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 that was negligently parked in the middle of the said road without putting any indicators or signal opposite to La-Classic Hotel, Yadavanahalli village, Hosur - Bengaluru NH-7 road, Bengaluru and thereby sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was rushed to Best Hospital, Bengoauru, where he has taken treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgery.
He has spent Rs.2 lakhs towards his treatment.
Further at the time of accident he was working as driver and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. and due to the accidental injuries he lost his earnings and also suffering permanent disabilities.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
9. In support of case of petitioner, petitioner himself stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 documents.

Per contra to falsify the case of the petitioner and to substantiate the defence of the respondent no.1,
their counsel had cross-examined PW1 at length.

In support of these contentions the respondent No.1 has examined its Assistant Legal Manager as RW.1.
10.
In order to prove the factum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 FIR, Ex.P.2 Complaint, Ex.P.3 Spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and Ex.P.7 Chargesheet.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Mohan Kumar (petitioner's son), the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of Venkatesh Alias Venkatesh Reddy vs Magma Hdi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175877925/
3 Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666.
11.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 vehemently contended that as the petitioner was not having a driving licence to ride a motorcycle at the time of accident, certain degree of contributory negligence must be attributed to him.
In this regard the petitioner has produced his DL which is marked as Ex.P.8.
On perusal of the same it reflects that the petitioner has possessed valid DL on the date of accident.
12. In this regard perusal of the evidence makes it evident that the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 was parked in an endangered manner on the road.

Such act of the driver of the Eicher canter in parking the said vehicle in the middle of a busy road that too without putting on the indicators itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Further as per the say of the petitioner he came to know that as he could not control the vehicle as he had dashed the rear portion of offending vehicle.
The offending vehicle has caused accident to the other vehicle prior to this accident.
The previous accident had happened 10- 15 minutes prior to this accident.
Further the stationed vehicle was a mini truck.
The vehicle was parked in the middle lane of the highway and if the sign boards were displayed for the public / other persons of vehicle concern the accident would have not happened.

Under such circumstances it appears in all probability that by the time the petitioner realized that the Eicher vehicle was not mobile, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his motorcycle to avoid collision.
13. Though the respondent No.1 insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
No doubt, the Assistant Legal Manager of the said company was examined as RW.1 but his evidence is no way helpful to prove the defence of respondent No.1.
Because he is not an eye-witness to the accident and his evidence is not supported by any document.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer of the vehicle to displace the version of the accident as deposed by PW.1 in this case.
Hence the respondents No.1 utterly failed to discharge the burden that was placed on them.
Added to this the respondent No.1 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its insured Eicher vehicle who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.1.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of Eicher lorry has to be disbelieved.
With this observation, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 is proved.
In this view of the matter no iota of negligence can be attributed on the part of the petitioner in the occurrence of resultant accident.
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Eicher canter.
Therefore the he is entitled for compensation.

15. As per the contents of the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
(i) Lacerated wound left side face, fracture left spheroid bone, Fracture left orbit, Fracture of left maxillary sinus with haemoparitorium, Fracture left zygoma, Fracture of left TM joint and other injuries.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The Discharge summary issued by BEST Hospital, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 19.09.2022 to 21.09.2022 (3 days in total).
16.
The petitioner has deposed that on account of the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
So also the petitioner has not examined the doctor or produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact that he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that he has suffered permanent disability.
Therefore he is not entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of future income due to disability'.
In this case the petitioner has produced 23 medical bills as per Ex.P4 for having spent Rs.1,61,460/- towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
Anyhow because the petitioner has not proved that he has any kind of disability, compensation cannot be awarded under conventional heads.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the line of treatment and the medical expenses incurred by him, this tribunal is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the petitioner is awarded global compensation of Rs.2,50,000/-.

17. INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
18. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the second respondent.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Eicher canter bearing Reg.No.MH-10-DT-9666 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Out of the said compensation amount awarded, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized Bank/Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years (without any encumbrance or premature withdrawal) with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
